name: us-state-tax
description: ARKANSAS, WHOSE HIGHEST MARGINAL RATE IS 13.70% AND IS NOT IN ARKANSAS'S RATE SCHEDULE: A.C.A. 26-51-201 writes TWO rate schedules selected by INCOME rather than by filing status - below $94,700 of net taxable income the graduated table of 0%, 2%, 3%, 3.4% and 3.7%, and one dollar above it a different table charging 2% on the first $4,700 and 3.7% on every dollar above, applied to the WHOLE net income, less a bracket adjustment of $290 that falls by $10 for each further $100 of income - and a $10 relief withdrawn per $100 earned is TEN PERCENTAGE POINTS of marginal rate, so the band from $94,701 is taxed at 13.70% in 2026 and 13.90% in 2025 against top statutory rates of 3.7% and 3.9%, and nothing in any published Arkansas bracket table contains either figure; where the provision written to remove a cliff is ITSELF A STAIRCASE OF THIRTY, because its rows are $100 wide and its amounts whole dollars, so $10 of tax arrives on one cent of income 29 times in 2026 and 31 times in 2025 - Ohio has two such steps and was the only discontinuous rate structure here - and the 2026 adjustment OVERSHOOTS, so one dollar of extra income at $94,700 CUTS the bill by $2.66 where the 2025 card undershoots the same join by $20.70; where a model built from the published bracket table alone, which is every account of this state, is too low by a FLAT $287.30 at every income above the band - $287.30 at $100,000 and $287.30 at $10,000,000, because both routes are linear with the same slope and the error is the whole adjustment - and $330.70 then $329.00 in 2025, the step being the card's own oddity of printing $3,809 plus 3.9% over $100,000, which makes one dollar of income worth $1.70 LESS tax; where the LOW INCOME TAX TABLES CHARGE THE POOREST ARKANSANS UP TO 12.40%, 3.35 times the top rate - seven tables of tax by state AGI and family size taken IN LIEU of the standard deduction, with implied marginal rates of 7.00% single, 9.40% head of household with no or one dependent, 10.40% and 10.77% joint, and 12.40% for a SINGLE PARENT OF TWO between $24,818 and $29,000, which is the steepest rate in the Arkansas income tax - and married filing separately is BARRED from all seven, so a separated Arkansan at $14,000 of AGI pays tax where a single filer pays nothing, which also makes them the only filer who can witness the bottom of the rate schedule at all; where the PUBLISHED CARD AND THE STATUTE DO NOT COMPUTE THE SAME TAX, because the card's reductions of $111.98, $223.97, $287.97 and $419.96 are each exactly the row's own rate short of the accumulated tax beneath - the card is anchored ONE DOLLAR BELOW each bracket floor - so every Arkansan above $5,600 pays the statutory tax plus two to four cents, and the instructions settle which governs: a formula's results must match the table; where 50% of net long-term capital gain is exempt under 26-51-815(a), the largest flat capital-gains exclusion here; where the $6,000 retirement exemption has NO AGE TEST and has not moved since 1997, reaching a 45-year-old, with military retired pay exempt in full outside it; and where the standard deduction is $2,470 for every status but joint, so A SINGLE PARENT GETS NO MORE DEDUCTION THAN A SINGLE FILER. Plus 1,033 local income taxes across 40 states: New York City, Yonkers, all 24 Maryland jurisdictions, all 92 Indiana counties, all 24 Michigan cities, all 679 municipalities and all 214 Ohio school districts - more taxing jurisdictions than the rest of the United States put together. Zero dependencies, MIT, ESM and CommonJS, TypeScript types included.

scripts.build: rm -rf dist && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.cjs.json && node scripts/finalize.mjs
